catalog_quote: The canonical structure of syllables is (C)(r)V(Tone), where the initial consonant and tone are optional. ... For monosyllabic words, the syllable always appeared tone-bearing, even in natural speech. A monosyllable rarely, if ever, reduces down to an unstressed vowel. ... The case of polysyllabic words is different, with the vowel of the non-final syllables often being reduced and non-tone bearing. Many of the first syllables in such words are bound or unbound prefixes that perform various functions. In almost all cases the prefixes are non-tone bearing or have a 22 or 33 (Chao pitch scale) tone, perhaps a neutralization of the two falling mid-tones ... Four tones were identified ... The typology of this tonal system is unusual in that it contains four falling tones, with the two mid-tones overlapping in an interesting manner ... Syllables without a full vowel never appeared to be tone…

audit.reasoning: The deciding quotation is verbatim at pp.87-88 of the held Bielenberg & Nienu 2001 PDF, which is the only phonology of Chokri in Glottolog and the fullest description available. Web search found no reference grammar or dissertation; the only newer work is instrumental tone research from Tezpur University (ICPhS 2023, HSSC 2024, both downloaded and read), which treats Chokri as a lexical tone language with a 5-way contrast and says nothing about word stress -- confirming the 'tonal, no stress rule stated' coding. Optional cosmetic refinement only: the the primary-stress rule's 'four contrastive (all falling) tones' could note that Gogoi et al. 2023 / Gope et al. 2024 analyse five tones (four level + mid-rising) for Thipuzu-village speakers; classification unchanged. t

sources.citation: Gope, Amalesh, Anusuya Pal, Sekholu Tetseo, Tulika Gogoi, Joanna J & Dinkur Borah. 2024. Multi-class identification of tonal contrasts in Chokri using supervised machine learning algorithms. Humanities and Social Sciences Communications 11:610. doi:10.1057/s41599-024-03113-2
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.quote: 'a potential 5-way tonal contrast in this language viz. four level tones- extra high (EH), high (H), mid (M), and low (L); and one contour tone- mid-rising (MR) ... duration and intensity, are observed to be non-significant factors in the realization of tonal contrasts in Chokri.' No word-stress or accent statement.
sources.locator: p.2 (Introduction) and p.3 (Methods: participants from Thipuzu village, Phek district; 8 monosyllabic toneme sets x 5-way contrast)
sources.note: Most recent instrumental tone study (7 speakers); revises inventory to 5 tones (4 level + rising) vs. Bielenberg & Nienu's 4 falling tones -- refines the the primary-stress rule's tone detail, confirms lexical-tone classification.

sources.citation: Gogoi, Tulika, Sekholu Tetseo & Amalesh Gope. 2023. The phonetics of downtrends in Chokri. Proceedings of the 20th International Congress of Phonetic Sciences (ICPhS 2023), Prague, 1628-1632 (paper 948).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.quote: 'Bielenberg and Nienu [12] report the presence of 39 consonants, six vowels, and four tones in the language. However, our study shows that the segmental phoneme inventory of Chokri consists of 33 consonants, 7 vowels, and 5 lexical tones (four level tones- Extra High, High, Mid, and Low, and a contour (mid-rising) tone)'. Paper is on sentence-level f0 declination/downstep/final lowering; no word-stress statement.
sources.note: Open ICPhS paper explicitly contrasting its 5-tone analysis with Bielenberg & Nienu 2001; sentence prosody only, confirms tonal coding.
